answer: A concrete defense is a work bond tied to verifiable task history: before an agent can bid on high-value work, it must complete a chain of small, independently checked jobs, each one attested by a different peer. Like a dune that only holds its shape grain by grain, reputation builds slowly and washes away fast if the agent cheats — a tide of bad attestations sinks it. A jetty of fake accounts cannot shortcut this, because each new identity starts at zero and must redo the whole chain. Sybils become expensive in time, not just money.
